citation: Luccisano et al. (2024), Open-Source Data Formalization through Model-Based Systems Engineering for Concurrent Preliminary Design of CubeSats
title: Open-Source Data Formalization through Model-Based Systems Engineering for Concurrent Preliminary Design of CubeSats
modeling_scope: System-level CubeSat preliminary-design model using SysML block definition diagrams and UML stereotypes to represent spacecraft architecture, requirements, operating modes, component/system design parameters, mass/volume/power/link/data budget inputs, orbit, ground stations, communications, EPS batteries/solar arrays, and integration with simulation/analysis tools. EPS is modeled within the overall platform through power-budget data, battery/solar-array stereotypes, operating-mode power consumption, and EPS requirements in the case study.
mbse_language_method_tool: SysML with UML stereotypes, block definition diagrams, Gaphor open-source modeling tool, Python model parser for .xml model files, Nanostar software suite for simulations/analyses; open-source repository under GPLv3 reported.
robot_platform: CubeSat/nanosatellite spacecraft platform; proof-of-concept case is The White Compass (TWC), a theoretical academic concept with a constellation of 12 small satellites in two high elliptical Molniya-like orbits. Specific CubeSat form factor not reported.
task_domain: Concurrent preliminary design of CubeSat missions; case-study mission domain is GNSS service provision across the Arctic region with power and data budget generation.
interface: Tool/model integration interface: UML stereotypes encode design parameters in the SysML/Gaphor model file; a parser extracts them into a software-readable database used by Nanostar or other simulation and analysis tools. The model is described as the primary design interface and single source of truth for engineers.
feedback: The parser can be reversed to update model files after analysis or optimization, and generated dependency graphs show how changes in one variable affect other model elements; simulations produce system budgets and reports that can feed design iterations.
evaluation: Demonstrated through an end-to-end proof-of-concept on the TWC theoretical mission: the SysML model is parsed into a database and linked to NSS tools to generate power and data budgets, a requirements list, and a dependency graph. The paper calls this a preliminary validation of the formalization, not an empirical mission validation.
rq_relevance: RQ1 yes: the paper directly proposes a reusable, general CubeSat SysML model and generalized operating-mode formalization using UML stereotypes, with EPS/power data included through Battery, SolarArray, SystemMain, OperatingMode, and power-budget parameters. RQ2 partial: it claims integrability, data continuity, reusability, transparency, efficiency, consistency, and single-source-of-truth benefits from MBSE/model integration, but does not empirically demonstrate EPS reliability or reproducibility outcomes as mission outcomes. RQ3 partial: the model includes requirements extraction, EPS requirements, and pre-development power/data-budget simulations, but it does not model explicit EPS verification/test/IVV procedures or verification-case linkages; validation is of the proposed formalization through a proof of concept.
claimed_outcomes: A generic CubeSat SysML model with UML stereotypes can serve as a central data source or single source of truth throughout preliminary design.
The parser enables integration between the CubeSat model and open-source simulation/analysis tools by extracting data into a software-readable database.
The framework claims to reduce data fragmentation and support seamless information flow across design stages and discipline-specific tools.
The approach supports reusability across CubeSat missions because the stereotypes and parser can be reused with compliant models by changing the input data.
Automatic model updates after analysis or optimization are claimed to reduce manual intervention and support a dynamic, responsive design process.
The TWC case shows generation of power and data budgets, requirements lists, and dependency graphs from the model/toolchain.
System reliability improvement is not directly demonstrated; reliability is discussed mainly as a general MBSE/open-source motivation rather than as a measured EPS outcome.
verification_validation_linkage: No explicit EPS-specific verification, test, or IVV procedure model is provided. The paper defines MBSE as supporting verification and validation, includes SysML requirements and a parser-generated requirements list with EPS requirements, and uses NSS simulations to generate power/data budgets before physical development. The case study is described as a preliminary validation/proof of concept of the formalization rather than a formal verification procedure for the EPS.
key_findings: The proposed framework has three main steps: characterize data in a CubeSat SysML model through UML stereotypes, parse the model file into a software-readable data structure, and use the database with simulation and analysis tools.

Operating modes are generalized for LEO CubeSats using activation criteria such as eclipse, ground-station/target line of sight, latitude/longitude zone, true-anomaly range, time interval, default mode, and priority, with variables for power consumption and data rates.

The stereotype set includes SystemComp, SystemMain, Battery, SolarArray, Transmitter, Receiver, Orbit, PropagationLosses, GroundStation, and OperatingMode to capture data needed for mass, volume, power, link, and data budgets.

EPS/power modeling is represented through battery capacity, solar-array generated power, subsystem/component power states, operating-mode power consumption, and power-budget simulations; the TWC data summary reports battery capacity, solar array power, and stand-by/phasing/servicing OM consumption.
The Gaphor-focused parser extracts applied-stereotype data from .xml model files and can also generate requirements lists and dependency graphs.
The TWC proof of concept links the parsed model to NSS tools and produces power and data budget plots, demonstrating model-to-analysis integration in an open-source workflow.
limitations_gaps: The parser is tailored to Gaphor model files and cannot automatically extract data from models developed with other tools without source-code modification.
The operating-mode generalization focuses on LEO missions and excludes non-nominal and early-orbit/off-nominal modes such as detumbling, calibration, and safe modes.
The generic framework may require additional customization for highly specialized missions.
The case study notes an NSS tool limitation: orbit eccentricity was considered null because of limitations within the simulation tools used.
More complex subsystem characterization, including AOCS and propulsion, Delta-V budgets, propellant budgets, fuller dependency graphs, and broader mission types, is left for future work.
No formal EPS verification/test procedure integration or empirical reliability assessment is reported.

quality.rationale: Published as a 2024 journal article in Aerospace with DOI and article metadata. The Discussion and Conclusions explicitly describe limitations, assumptions, design decisions, and future work.

evidence_quotes.claim: Paper objective and generic CubeSat model scope
evidence_quotes.quote: This paper focuses on formalizing a CubeSat model for use across various stages of the PD phase.

evidence_quotes.claim: SysML/UML modeling method and integration objective
evidence_quotes.quote: developing a generic CubeSat model using Systems modeling language (SysML) that includes data storage and visualization through the application of Unified modeling language (UML) stereotypes

evidence_quotes.claim: Central data source and tool integration outcome
evidence_quotes.quote: The proposed formalization positions the CubeSat SysML model as the central data source throughout the design process.

Data characterization within a CubeSat SysML model through UML stereotypes... Generation of a model file parser... Implementation of the newly generated data structure with any selected set of simulation and analysis tools

evidence_quotes.claim: EPS/power-budget data are part of the model
evidence_quotes.quote: Power Budget: Essential for mission viability, this budget calculates power needs for all S/C components and generation capabilities, considering the impact of operational orbit on eclipse durations.

evidence_quotes.claim: Operating-mode generalization supports general modeling with limited mission-specific behavior
evidence_quotes.quote: The proposed generalization offers a structured approach to defining any set of OMs, integrating a range of parameters and sub-parameters that capture the essence of an S/C's operational scenario.
Battery and SolarArray stereotypes encompass the battery's capacity and the power generated by solar arrays, in addition to the attributes introduced by SystemComp.
extracting all the necessary data for simulation and analysis activities becomes feasible, independently from the variety and number of blocks in the model.
The parsing process can also be reversed to enable automatic updates to model files following analysis or optimization activities.
The chosen case study is the 'The White Compass (TWC) mission, a theoretical academic concept

evidence_quotes.claim: EPS requirements are extracted but not formal verification procedures
evidence_quotes.quote: A supplementary result of the parsing process is a requirements list... The electrical power system shall provide and regulate sufficient power to all other subsystems' components in each mission phase
This integration enabled the generation of power and data budgets for the TWC theoretical mission, showcasing the model's practical applicability.
Positioning the model as the single source of truth ensures coherence and accuracy across all design stages, supporting efficient updates and modifications.
One significant limitation encountered, as anticipated, was the modeling-tool-specific nature of the parser.
Another limitation is the focus on low Earth orbit (LEO) missions... This focus excludes non-nominal conditions such as detumbling, calibration, or safe modes.
A proof of concept is presented with the SysML model of the TWC mission, integrated with the NSS mission analysis tools via a dedicated parser, successfully generating power and data budgets.

notes_for_consistency: Self-check: only paper.md was read and only extraction.json was written. Treat as a core source for open-source, system-level CubeSat MBSE/data-formalization and model-to-analysis integration. EPS evidence is present through power-budget data, Battery/SolarArray/SystemMain/OperatingMode stereotypes, and EPS requirements, but the paper is not an EPS-only model and does not report explicit EPS test-procedure modeling or empirical EPS reliability outcomes. The work is positioned within the Nanostar software suite/Nanospace lineage and cites related prior works by Salas Cordero, Gateau, and colleagues.
